messages:
marta_devex: Heads-up — a user hit this when trying `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo.git@main` on macOS ARM, Python 3.11:
```
ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk, which is required to install pyproject.toml-based projects
```
They also said `from redwood import AsyncClient` raised ImportError after installing the wheel. Works for us with `pip install -e .`.

ishaan_eng: Thanks. Two likely causes: (1) pip-from-vcs + poetry-core can fail on older pip/build versions; (2) editable installs hide packaging/export issues (modules present on disk). Do we still rely on poetry-core as the build-backend?

natalie_pkg: Yes pyproject currently uses `poetry-core`. Quick checklist I ran locally: py.typed missing, async export not re-exported at package top-level, and MANIFEST/pyproject include not set so sdist omits typing marker.

support_bot: CI packaging job failed on PR #1529 with similar wheel error on macos-arm64: https://ci.internal/logs/1529

ishaan_eng: Minimal fixes to unblock users fast:
- Add `redwood/py.typed` and include it in MANIFEST.in (or tool.poetry.include) so typing consumers get the marker.
- Export AsyncClient at `redwood/__init__.py`: `from .client import Client
from .async_client import AsyncClient
__all__ = ["Client","AsyncClient"]`.
- Either switch `pyproject.build-system` to `setuptools>=61, wheel` for better VCS install compatibility or document the requirement `pip>=23` when using poetry-core.

marta_devex: Good. What do we give users as a short workaround while we ship a patch wheel?

natalie_pkg: Workaround I gave a user: upgrade pip/build and install wheel locally:
```
python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel build
python -m build
pip install dist/redwood-*.whl
```
For poetry users: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt && pip install -r reqs.txt` — that avoids `pip install git+...` resolver issues.

ishaan_eng: Also recommend publishing wheels for macOS/arm and manylinux/aarch64 using cibuildwheel in the release pipeline so consumer pip doesn't try to compile native deps. Longer-term follow-up.

ci-bot: PR #1529 updated with packaging changes (exports + manifest). CI re-run queued.

marta_devex: Can we add a tiny CI smoke test that creates a clean venv, `pip install dist/*.whl`, then runs:
`python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient; import pkgutil; print(bool(pkgutil.get_data('redwood','py.typed')))"`
so we catch regressions where editable differs from wheel?

natalie_pkg: Yep, I'll add `tests/test_packaging_imports.py` with that snippet and a packaging step in CI. Also will add a short note to INSTALL.md about VCS installs and pip minimum.

support_bot: I've updated the support ticket with the workaround commands and asked the user to try the wheel route. Will ping again once CI publishes a patch wheel.

marta_devex: Thanks — small fixes + docs + CI test should reduce onboarding friction. Will follow up if users still see failures. :rocket:
